evidence: src/domain/errors/DomainErrors.ts: abstract class DomainError with abstract code; ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError, InvalidStatusTransitionError all extend DomainError
src/domain/inventory/StockReservationService.ts imports InsufficientStockError from '../errors/DomainErrors' and throws it in reserve()
src/domain/inventory/StockReservationService.ts reserve(): checks product.canReserve(quantity) for every allocation before calling product.reserve(quantity), so the stock rule stays in Product
src/domain/inventory/StockReservationService.ts release()/commit() pass the work to product.release/product.commit and don't repeat its logic
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain unit has two files that work together. DomainErrors.ts defines the domain's error types: the DomainError base class with a code, plus ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidStatusTransitionError. StockReservationService.ts handles stock reservation across several products and uses the module's own InsufficientStockError rather than ad-hoc errors. The stock-availability rule is not duplicated. The service calls Product.canReserve and Product.reserve/release/commit, so the rule stays with Product. The only thing the service adds is all-or-nothing ordering across products. Product may also throw InsufficientStockError inside reserve (Product.ts depends on DomainErrors.ts), but that can't be confirmed here, and the rule itself is still defined only by canReserve. Neither file bypasses the module's abstractions or splits into unrelated concerns.
